title: Estimating Baseflow Recession Constants from Sparse Gauge Records

headings.text: Estimating Baseflow Recession Constants from Sparse Gauge Records

key_sentences: We present a simple resampling procedure that recovers the recession constant from sparse records.
Tested on 41 catchments, the method reduced the median estimation error from 31% to 9% relative to a naive fit.
Reliable values of k are needed to forecast low flows and to size water supply storage.
In many regions, however, gauges are read manually and the record contains only a handful of values each month.
The correction fits the recession constant to many random subsets of the thinned record and then adjusts the median fit with a bias factor calibrated on the daily series.
As the sampling interval grows, the naive fit overestimates the recession constant, because slow late-recession flows are over-represented among the retained points.
The corrected estimate stays within 10% of the daily-data value for all intervals up to 15 days.
Sparse gauge records can support reliable recession analysis if the sampling bias is corrected.
